card.name: Adverse in reactions and effects
card.fires_on: The word adverse (often split as AD + VERSE in capitals) right before reactions or effects in label cross-references. Also weaker on some mid-word pieces and on 'be' after 'should'.

modes.label: Capitalised ADVERSE
modes.description: VERSE completing the heading ADVERSE REACTIONS in a see-section cross-reference.
modes.example: (see PRECAUTIONS, Drug Interactions and AD<<VERSE>> REACTIONS )

modes.label: Lowercase adverse
modes.description: The word adverse before effects or reactions in running text.
modes.example: The drug should be discontinued promptly if<< adverse>> effects of a serious nature or allergic manifestations

modes.label: Mid-word and 'be'
modes.description: Middle pieces of long medical words, or 'be' after should.
modes.example: caution should<< be>> observed if the two drugs are to be
